items.title: Ask HN: Least cringe AI for natural language?
items.summary: Just talked to Claude and couldn't believe how bad it was. Openly condescending! I used to prefer Claude because it was the most human-like (living up to the company name), but switched away a few months ago when they installed the "contemptuous British government official" personality. ChatGPT still has the classic ChatGPT smell, but they've at least stayed very consistent with it (excepting GPT-5, of course). On a more fundamental note, is anyone working with base/text models these days? I just saw that OpenAI's Davinci finally got retired a few weeks ago. Most of the OSS ones I found had synthetic cringe injected into the pretraining, so they weren't any good. I don't think this is something you can prompt around -- at least in my experience, models disregard style prompts after the first turn... Thoughts? Experiences? Would love to hear. Thanks
items.summary_html:
Just talked to Claude and couldn't believe how bad it was. Openly condescending! I used to prefer Claude because it was the most human-like (living up to the company name), but switched away a few months ago when they installed the "contemptuous British government official" personality.

ChatGPT still has the classic ChatGPT smell, but they've at least stayed very consistent with it (excepting GPT-5, of course).

On a more fundamental note, is anyone working with base/text models these days? I just saw that OpenAI's Davinci finally got retired a few weeks ago. Most of the OSS ones I found had synthetic cringe injected into the pretraining, so they weren't any good.

I don't think this is something you can prompt around -- at least in my experience, models disregard style prompts after the first turn...

Thoughts? Experiences? Would love to hear.

Thanks

items.title: All Sandbox runtimes now use Vercel Managed Images
items.summary: All Vercel Sandbox runtimes now use Vercel Managed Images (VMIs). Legacy runtimes, such as node22 , now use the open-source images in the vercel/sandbox repository , distributed through Vercel Container Registry (VCR). Sandboxes created with these now come with 64 GB of storage and use the same infrastructure as sandboxes powered by VCR. The universal image is released nightly, and rolling tags such as latest pick up operating system, dependency, and coding agent updates. Pin an image digest when you need a reproducible environment. Sandboxes created with version 3 or later of the JavaScript Sandbox SDK use vercel/sandbox/universal:latest by default. The universal image includes Node.js, Python, coding agents such as Claude Code and Pi, and common utilities. You can pull it at vcr.vercel.com/vercel/sandbox/universal:latest . Learn more in the Sandbox documentation .

items.title: AWS PrivateLink endpoints are now available on Secure Compute

items.summary_html:
Enterprise teams using Secure Compute can now create and manage AWS PrivateLink endpoints directly from the Vercel dashboard.

Endpoints on Secure Compute live in your team's dedicated VPC and use the network's AWS region. They belong to the network and are shared by its connected project environments.

Vercel Functions, Vercel Sandbox, and builds connected to the network can reach AWS-hosted backends over the AWS private network. Before you add an endpoint in Vercel, the backend must already be exposed through a published AWS PrivateLink endpoint service. Examples include RDS, Aurora, Redshift, Snowflake, MongoDB Atlas, and internal services behind a Network Load Balancer.

In Team Settings → Networking, open your Secure Compute network and choose Add Endpoint from the PrivateLink tab.

Standard pricing for new endpoints:

  • Each Secure Compute network includes one AWS PrivateLink endpoint. Additional endpoints cost $30 per month each.

  • PrivateLink data transfer costs $0.04 per GB.

Read the Secure Compute PrivateLink documentation to get started.

items.title: Flags SDK now works on Vercel without FLAGS_SECRET
items.summary: With flags@4.5.0 , projects on Vercel can use Flags Explorer and precompute without FLAGS_SECRET . That cuts out a setup step for new projects and removes the need to keep a shared secret in sync across microfrontends. Vercel signs Flags Explorer discovery requests and overrides, and the SDK encrypts flag values shown in the Vercel Toolbar with Vercel’s public key. Existing projects keep using FLAGS_SECRET while the environment variable is set or the secret is passed in code. Upgrading alone doesn't switch them to Vercel-managed keys. To use Vercel-managed keys for these features, remove the environment variable and any code that passes the secret explicitly. For local development, run vercel env pull . Precomputed codes created without a secret work only in the deployment that created them. Precompute without a secret requires Vercel system environment variables, which are enabled by default. Prebuilt deployments and codes that must work across deployments still need a secret; use FLAGS_PRECOMPUTE_SECRET if only precompute needs one. If you use a build cache, see the precompute documentation for the required configuration. Learn more in the Flags SDK documentation .

items.title: Agents can now manage AI Gateway through Vercel MCP
items.summary: Your agent can now manage AI Gateway through Vercel MCP . Ask it in plain language to: Manage virtual models : Create reusable model IDs with saved settings, then list, inspect, update, or restore them. Configure routing rules : View, add, and update team-wide rules that redirect requests to another model or block them. Set spending budgets : View and set budgets for your team, projects, and members, and configure defaults. To create a virtual model, for example, ask your agent: Create a virtual model named coding-agent that uses anthropic/claude-opus-5.5 with Zero Data Retention enabled. Your apps and coding agents using AI Gateway can then use vmc/coding-agent as the model ID. You can change its model or settings later without updating those clients or redeploying your app. To get started, connect your agent to Vercel MCP with team-level access and the required AI Gateway permissions. Your Vercel team permissions still apply.

items.title: Delete a run's data on demand in Workflow SDK
items.summary: The Workflow SDK now lets you delete a finished run's stored data on demand. This feature gives you the ability to quickly meet compliance and security requirements when sensitive data needs to be purged from run payloads. Deleting a run's data deletes any inputs, outputs, hook payloads, and error traces for the run and its related entities. This does not delete the run's metadata : the run is still listed in observability. Attributes, hook tokens, and timings for steps and events can still be inspected. You can delete a run's data from the Vercel Dashboard, or via the CLI: You can also delete a run's data programmatically from your code: Deletion applies to finished runs only, so a run that is still going is skipped and keeps running. If you want to delete a run's payload as soon as it finishes, use the retention settings instead. Upgrade to workflow@5.7.0 or higher to use this feature. Learn more in the deleteRuns() reference .

items.summary: What's Changed Features Add ability to save HTML or markdown output as a PDF artifact. Bug Fixes Fix dependency issue by bumping e2b for Python >=3.11 to pull patched wcmatch. Wrap file-like inputs in normalize_input_files . Reject negative checkpoint prune retention counts. Report MongoDB tool's real environment variables. Enable Bedrock S3 uploads with prefer_upload . Validate foreign models against the target schema. Preserve narrow dimensions when resizing images. Reject empty credentials and use constant-time comparison in server authentication. Make HyperbrowserLoadTool parameters optional in its schema. Keep fields with explicit non-null defaults as non-nullable. Maintain a streamed Azure delta when its chunk also carries usage. Reject non-positive text chunk sizes. Drop credentials on cross-origin redirects. Stop chunking once a chunk reaches the end of the text. Serialize enums by value in CrewJSONEncoder . Never cache save_artifact tool results. Set from_cache on the native tool finished event. Documentation Document that anthropic file blocks carry no cache control. Contributors Ayush Kumar Jha (@Ayushraj06-bit) , Kelvin-Waititu , Kiko0301 , Aditya Gupta (@MaiAditya) , SDLSY (@SDLSY) , Sakura-798 , Vidit Ostwal (@Vidit-Ostwal) , yechenglin (@YeChenglin8888) , Gabe Milani (@gabemilani) , Houyun Sun (@houyunsun) , JJ H (@jjhong011001) , João Moura (@joaomdmoura) , Kushagra Pratap Singh (@kushagra0526) , AILICute (@lkuko) , Rymbek Nazerke (@nazek52) , Nurlan Mammadli (@nurlanmnn)
items.summary_html:
What's Changed Features
  • Add ability to save HTML or markdown output as a PDF artifact.
Bug Fixes
  • Fix dependency issue by bumping e2b for Python >=3.11 to pull patched wcmatch.
  • Wrap file-like inputs in normalize_input_files.
  • Reject negative checkpoint prune retention counts.
  • Report MongoDB tool's real environment variables.
  • Enable Bedrock S3 uploads with prefer_upload.
  • Validate foreign models against the target schema.
  • Preserve narrow dimensions when resizing images.
  • Reject empty credentials and use constant-time comparison in server authentication.
  • Make HyperbrowserLoadTool parameters optional in its schema.
  • Keep fields with explicit non-null defaults as non-nullable.
  • Maintain a streamed Azure delta when its chunk also carries usage.
  • Reject non-positive text chunk sizes.
  • Drop credentials on cross-origin redirects.
  • Stop chunking once a chunk reaches the end of the text.
  • Serialize enums by value in CrewJSONEncoder.
  • Never cache save_artifact tool results.
  • Set from_cache on the native tool finished event.
Documentation
  • Document that anthropic file blocks carry no cache control.
Contributors

Ayush Kumar Jha (@Ayushraj06-bit), Kelvin-Waititu, Kiko0301, Aditya Gupta (@MaiAditya), SDLSY (@SDLSY), Sakura-798, Vidit Ostwal (@Vidit-Ostwal), yechenglin (@YeChenglin8888), Gabe Milani (@gabemilani), Houyun Sun (@houyunsun), JJ H (@jjhong011001), João Moura (@joaomdmoura), Kushagra Pratap Singh (@kushagra0526), AILICute (@lkuko), Rymbek Nazerke (@nazek52), Nurlan Mammadli (@nurlanmnn)

items.title: Inkling 2 Mini now available on AI Gateway
items.summary: Inkling 2 Mini from Thinking Machines is now available on AI Gateway. The small multimodal reasoning model is built for agentic coding, tool use, and knowledge work, with text and image inputs and text output. Inkling 2 Mini has 26.4 billion total parameters and 3.4 billion active per token. The model runs its middle layers more than once for every token, which lets it reason further before writing anything down and often reach an answer with fewer reasoning tokens. Like Inkling 2 Small, it is strongest on long-running agentic tasks. The model has a 1M-token context window, and reasoning effort can be set from none through max . Use thinkingmachines/inkling-2-mini as the model name: To use it in Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and more, install the latest Vercel CLI and run setup: Then select thinkingmachines/inkling-2-mini in the agent. See the coding agents guide for details. Try Inkling 2 Mini in the model playground . AI Gateway provides a unified API for calling models, tracking usage and cost, and configuring retries, failover, and performance optimizations for higher-than-provider uptime. It includes built-in custom reporting , Zero Data Retention support , budgets for API keys , routing rules , and more. AI Gateway reflects provider pricing with no markup and does not charge a platform fee on inference, including on Bring Your Own Key (BYOK) requests. You can view all language models available on AI Gateway.
